saints.name: St. Walburga
saints.title: Abbess
saints.shortBlurb: An English nun who crossed to Germany to help St. Boniface, and ruled the double monastery of Heidenheim as abbess…
biography: Born about 710 in Devon, Walburga was the daughter of the West Saxon under-king Richard and of Winna, a sister of St. Boniface, and sister of Saints Willibald and Winnibald. At eleven she was left in the double monastery of Wimborne in Dorset when her father and brothers went on pilgrimage to Rome, and she spent twenty-six years there as a nun.

About 748 Boniface summoned her with other English nuns to the German mission. After a time under St. Lioba at Bischofsheim she was called to the double monastery of Heidenheim, where her brother Winnibald governed the monks; on his death in 761 she took charge of both communities as abbess.

Learned and beloved, she ruled until her death on 25 February 779. In 870 her relics were translated to Eichstatt, where a healing oil was held to flow from them, and Pope Adrian II canonized her on 1 May of that year; the feast of that translation, kept on May Eve, gave the name 'Walpurgis Night' to the folklore of Germany.
saints.knownFor: Governing the monastery of Heidenheim in the German mission.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 25 February
